first.text:
Draft refreshed and checked. Nothing is recorded yet. Here is what adopting would do, item by item, then the three things it flags.

**1. Pull-up dose**

The pull-up's weekly target now counts negatives and band pull-ups as its own sets, and the note we had left excusing the old target of 1 is gone. I've proposed **10 hard sets a week**. Reasoning:

- The band for a priority lift is 5–15, stock default 8. Your week as written plans 3 negatives, 7 band sets and the strict single: 11. A target of 10 sits just under what the week already holds, so it opens the block rather than capping it, and it keeps the honest signal — the last two Wednesdays delivered 5 and 4 sets, not 11, and a target of 10 will say so if that keeps happening rather than hide it.
- If you'd rather the target reflect what has actually been landing while sleep settles, 8 is the defensible alternative: still inside the band, and the week only has to be three-quarters done to meet it.

Your call: 10 or 8. The dry run shows the target cleanly inside the band either way; nothing else about the pull-up work changes.

**2. Kettlebell swings**

The swings leave Monday's lifting and become their own conditioning session on Monday, beside the lift:

- 12 minutes, one set at the top of each minute, 12 reps, 40 lb (18.1 kg), effort around 7 of 10.
- When a session comes in at or under that effort, the next one adds 2 minutes, up to 16; once you're at 16, reps climb toward 15.
- Monday's lifting estimate drops from 58 to 47 minutes of the 75 available.
- Monday 2 Nov's logged workout is untouched; the swings you did as a finisher stay exactly where you logged them.

On counting: a session set up as conditioning is read as conditioning time, not as lifting sets, so its swings won't land in anyone's hard-set total. That's what the rules say; I'll confirm it against the first week that closes after this is adopted. One thing to expect: doing the swings in the same visit as the lift is effectively still the finisher, just on its own clock, and the weekly plan may remark on a hard conditioning bout sharing a lifting day. If it does, that's a one-line note, not a reason to move them.

**3. The circuit**

Unchanged, as asked. I re-checked this week's plan under the new rules: a standing session is no longer judged against the day's lifting, so the same-day note for the circuit doesn't come up and there's nothing to excuse weekly from here on.

**What it flags**

- **Deadlift target is 4, below the 5–15 band.** Not new (it was in the first program) but it was hidden behind the pull-up's larger departure, and now it shows. Two honest options: (a) count Friday's Romanian deadlift toward the deadlift, the same way negatives now count toward the pull-up, and set the target at 6 — the week plans 4 deadlift sets plus 3 RDL sets, so 7; or (b) keep 4 and say why: the deadlift is the costliest lift to recover from, Tuesday's PT sometimes adds pulls, and the hinge gets its volume from the RDL. I lean to (a); it's the same fix you asked for on the pull-up. Tell me which.
- **One Hevy routine has drifted from this week's plan** — reps on three later sets of its first exercise and weights on the first three sets of its second; it looks like Monday's. Nothing to do now: it resolves when a week is next pushed, which waits on publish anyway.
- **The strict pull-up single as a held test, not a progressing line.** Already excused in the first program; the same note carries over.

Give me the pull-up target (10 or 8) and the deadlift choice (count the RDL at 6, or keep 4 with the reason), and I'll re-check and adopt on your yes. Not publishing.
